blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Applying AI and data ethics in practice means asking a short list of questions before any new project goes live. Is the data allowed to be used for this purpose? Are the people in the data represented fairly? Can the system explain its output to a non-technical reviewer? And what happens when it gets something wrong?

Provided that these questions have clear answers, the project can usually proceed. Where any answer is missing or uncomfortable, the project is either reshaped or paused until the gap is addressed. This is not a legal discussion; it is a judgement conversation, held early, while there is still time to change the design.

Although regulators are starting to ask these questions formally, the most serious risk is not the regulator. It is the quiet loss of customer trust when a badly designed system treats real people unfairly — and the story eventually becomes public.

items.q: According to the text, when should the ethics questions be asked?
options: Only when a regulator requests it
Once customer trust has been lost
Before any new project goes live
After the project has gone live
items.why: "asking a short list of questions before any new project goes live."

items.q: What happens when an answer is missing or uncomfortable?
options: The project proceeds under legal review
The project is reshaped or paused until the gap is addressed
items.why: "the project is either reshaped or paused until the gap is addressed."

items.q: The author calls this "a judgement conversation, not a legal discussion." This suggests that…
options: the decision is about values and design choices, not just compliance
the conversation can be skipped if the law allows it
items.why: Inferência: "judgement conversation, held early" — trata-se de escolhas de valor e design, decididas antes, não só de cumprir a lei.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: As long as a system is legal, its ethics do not need reviewing.
A fairness gap should be addressed before launch.
Losing customer trust is harder to fix than passing an audit.
Ethics questions are best asked while the design can still change.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que o maior risco não é o regulador, mas a perda de confiança — legalidade não basta.

items.q: What does the text imply about the timing of an ethics review?
options: Doing it early is what makes it useful, because the design can still be changed
It matters little as long as it happens eventually
It should wait until the system is fully built
It should only follow a public complaint
items.why: Inferência: "held early, while there is still time to change the design" — o valor está em fazê-lo enquanto a mudança ainda é possível.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte conduzindo uma revisão de ética sobre uma IA de pontuação de clientes. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for walking me through the model. It's clearly well built, and I can see the team has put a lot of work into the accuracy. But before we schedule the launch, I want to stop on one thing.

When I broke the scores down by customer group, the system was noticeably harder on newer accounts from smaller markets. Nobody designed it to do that. It simply learned the pattern from the historical data, where those accounts had thinner records. So the model is being fair to the data — but not fair to the people.

Here's my concern. If we go live and a real customer is scored badly for a reason we can't explain to them, that's not a technical bug. That's a trust problem, and trust is the one thing we can't patch later.

So I'm not killing the project. I'm pausing the launch. I'd like the team to reshape how those thin-record accounts are handled, and to make sure a non-technical reviewer can read the output and understand why a score came out the way it did. Give me two weeks, and let's do this properly the first time.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What problem did Charlotte find when she broke the scores down by customer group?
options: The model was slower for larger markets
The scores were identical across every group
The engineering team had faked the accuracy figures
The system was noticeably harder on newer accounts from smaller markets
items.why: "the system was noticeably harder on newer accounts from smaller markets."

items.q: Why does Charlotte say the model behaves this way?
options: Someone deliberately programmed it to penalise those accounts
The data was entered incorrectly by the team
It learned the pattern from historical data where those accounts had thinner records
items.why: "It simply learned the pattern from the historical data, where those accounts had thinner records."

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by "fair to the data — but not fair to the people"?
options: The people in the team disagreed with each other
The model followed the historical pattern faithfully, yet that pattern is unjust to real customers
The model ignored the data entirely
items.why: Inferência: reproduzir fielmente um padrão enviesado dos dados é ser justo com os dados, mas injusto com as pessoas.

items.q: What is Charlotte's decision about the project?
options: She is handing it to the regulator
She is pausing the launch, not killing the project
She is approving it as it is
items.why: "I'm not killing the project. I'm pausing the launch."

items.q: What does "trust is the one thing we can't patch later" suggest about her priorities?
options: She wants to delegate the decision to engineering
She sees lost customer trust as far harder to repair than a technical fault
She thinks trust is irrelevant to the project
She values a quick launch above everything else
items.why: Inferência: ao contrastar com um "bug", ela sinaliza que confiança perdida não se conserta como código — é o risco mais sério.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We need to apply these ethics questions to every launch, not just the sensitive ones." To apply here means to…
items.why: Apply = aplicar, pôr em prática o critério em cada projeto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Before launch, run through a short ___ of questions: consent, fairness, explainability and failure."
items.why: "a short list of questions" — lista curta de verificação antes do lançamento.

items.q: "The data was collected for billing, so using it for scoring is a different purpose." Purpose means…
options: the legal owner of the data
the goal or use something is intended for
items.why: Purpose = finalidade; a razão para a qual algo é usado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A good system can explain its output to a ___ reviewer, in plain language."
items.why: "non-technical reviewer" — alguém sem formação técnica que precisa entender a decisão.

items.q: "Rather than scrap the project, we'll reshape how thin-record accounts are handled." To reshape means to…
items.why: Reshape = remodelar, mudar a forma sem abandonar o projeto.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em revisões de ética e lançamento de produtos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Legal still has to sign off on the launch." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two reviewers pushed back on the fairness assumptions." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — levantar objeções sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed to fix the bias, but the team never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Let's hold off on the launch until the fairness gap is closed." To hold off on means to…
items.why: Hold off on = adiar, segurar algo até que uma condição seja atendida.

items.q: "Cosmetic tweaks won't move the needle on fairness." This means they will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir uma diferença perceptível.
